reference_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_promotions
FROM (
  -- one row per promotion with products
  SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
) AS t
WHERE t.n_products > 20
alternatives:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_promotions
FROM (
  -- one row per promotion with more than 20 products
  SELECT promo_id
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 20
) AS t

WITH promo_sizes AS (
  -- one row per promotion with products
  SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_promotions
FROM promo_sizes
WHERE n_products > 20

other_way.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_promotions
FROM (
  -- one row per promotion with more than 20 products
  SELECT promo_id
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 20
) AS t
other_way.tradeoff: HAVING inside the derived table keeps only the big promotions there, so the outer query just counts rows.
